title: Edgar A. McMahon — rural mail carrier advice
text:
EDGAR A. McMAHON.

When a carrier picks up mail from a box, before accepting it, he is supposed to see that it is properly addressed and stamped. Now there are several boys and girls on Route 3 who, not thinking of this provision, purposely place letters and post cards in the mail box with the back of the first one to me and the next will be facing it but upside down and so on; as a result I am compelled to do a great deal of shuffling to see that each is stamped and properly addressed. Now handlers of mail are not supposed to read cards, but anybody knows that bright colors are easily caught by the eye, especially so when they are moving as being shuffled around to find the address side. So my advice to find the cautious, courting folks is to place all letters, and especially courting
notes: Article is cut off at bottom — text ends mid-sentence with 'especially courting'. Appears to be a notice or column from a rural mail carrier, likely Route 3 out of Savoy.
